newsitem.title: UK: SQUASH-JANSHER AIMS FOR SIXTH BRITISH OPEN.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-JANSHER AIMS FOR SIXTH BRITISH OPEN.

text.p: Jansher Khan heads into this week's British Open with records in mind.
The world number one needs no reminding of the achievements of fellow Pakistani Jahangir Khan, winner of 10 successive British Opens and six World Opens in the 1980s.
But Jansher wants to make his mark the other way around -- 10 world titles and six British.
He has collected eight worlds and five British crowns to date. Victory in the Cardiff final on April 6 would complete one half of his double.
"My most important target is the World Open because I have to win that twice more to equal Jahangir's run in the British Open," said Jansher.
"I have perhaps four or five more years to do it which makes one more British Open the easier of the two to achieve."
Jansher plays Irish champion Derek Ryan in the first round on Tuesday and then possibly Greek champion Paul Gregory.

In the last 16 he is due to meet England's world number four Simon Parke, although Egyptian teenager Ahmed Barada will be trying to improve on his five-game loss to Parke in the third-place play-off in the Super Series finals on Saturday.
The top half of the draw also includes England number one Chris Walker and Australian prospects Craig Rowland and Dan Jenson.

Australia also leads the bottom half of the draw with the second-seeded Rodney Eyles, world number eight Brett Martin and Anthony Hill, who is making his first tournament appearance since he was banned in Qatar last year.

Martin reached the Super Series final with some stunning attacking play only to be dismissed in 24 minutes by Jansher. The Australian faces former world number two Peter Marshall of England, who qualifies as a wild card after two years out of the game with chronic fatigue syndrome.
The women's event has been weakened by the withdrawal of the third-seeded Cassie Jackman of England with an ankle injury.
Her absence increased the chances of an all-Australian final between Michelle Martin and Sarah Fitz-Gerald, who became world champion in Kuala Lumpur in October.
